notes: Notes:
1 FAS 0210 is a non-degree credit-bearing course, and it is a graduation requirement. It counts for 2 non-degree credits, i.e. they do not count towards the
degree. However, this course can be waived upon a successful test-out.
2 All degree-seeking students must earn 2 SCH of Arabic language by taking one course from the list. Arabic courses are categorized depending on the
student’s high school diploma and prior Arabic proficiency level.
 Holders of the Moroccan baccalaureate take ARB 1241 without placement.
 Holders of a cultural mission baccalaureate in Morocco (French, Spanish, etc.) take one ARB course based on placement test results.
 Holders of international high school degrees with no prior Arabic language instruction take one ARA course based on placement test results.
3 French Requirements: Newly admitted students holding Moroccan baccalaureate must submit a valid certificate (EV@LANG & TEF TP) to
determine the number/level of French courses required. This should be done during the first or second semester of instruction.
● FRN 3210 is the exit level for holders of the Moroccan baccalaureate.
● To be exempted from all French classes, a student must earn C2 in TCF, DALF, EV@LANG & TEF TP. Exempted students receive a waiver
of the last requirement course FRN3210 with 2 credits.

● Holders of the Moroccan baccalaureate may need to take additional non-degree applicable French courses as prerequisites. In their first semester of study, LC students cannot take French classes. Important notes:
• Holders of the Moroccan baccalaureate must earn 2 SCH of French language by taking FRN 3210 as an exit level

• Holders of an International high school diploma or the French schools’ baccalaureate (la mission française) are not required to take French courses but must take any other language offered by the Language Center to fulfill GenEd language requirements.

• Students holding Moroccan baccalaureate must prove their proficiency in French or take a placement test to find the appropriate course level. Based on their test scores, they might be exempt from or need to complete one to four French courses.

• To ensure completion of French requirements by the end of their junior year, all non-French 2000-level courses will have FRN1308/FRN1208 as a corequisite, all non-French 3000-level courses will have FRN2310/FRN2210 as a corequisite, and all non-French
• Transfer students who join AUl after their junior year's first semester will be assessed on a case-by-case basis to determine an appropriate timeline for completion.

4 Students are required to complete a one-credit civic engagement component as part of their degree requirements. Completion of the Civic Engagement requirement is mandatory for all undergraduate students as a condition for graduation. Students may satisfy this requirement through one of the following options: CIP 2100 will bear one institutional credit hour. This gives students the option of taking either CIP or an SLP course.
• FYE 1102 is a prerequisite for CIP 2100 and before enrolling in CIP 2100, a student must complete a minimum of 60- hours of fieldwork that must be documented using the University's SLP-CIP form.

• A student wishing to go for CIP should contact the Civic Engagement Office for guidance on how to do and document the 60 hours as soon as he/she passes FYE 1102. Students who enroll in CIP 2100 before doing the 60 hours will be dropped from CIP2100. The Community Engagement Office will communicate the list of students to be dropped by to the Office of the

• Students can take either SLP or CIP 2100 to complete their civic engagement requirement for graduation (a minimum of 60 hours is required for CIP and a minimum of 40 hours for SLP). Though SLP may require fewer service hours than CIP, its higher academic rigor and focus on students using class learning to achieve positive impact on the community provides an equivalent civic engagement experience.

• SLP must be taken at the same time as the course to which it is connected. For example: if the course code is "ABC 2305", then its SLP will have the code "ABC 2105", and students will not be allowed to register for ABC 2105 unless they are simultaneously registered for ABC 2305.

• In line with best practice in Service or Civic-based learning, this means that the 1-credit SLP must be connected to an approved course and cannot take place independently from the course (SLP 1101 will no longer be offered).
